text:
Ravi (infra): heads-up: mid-tier dedicated pool eu-west1-b seeing large egress spikes since ~09:10UTC. Looks correlated with a tenant running heavy offline-embedding-batch jobs (tenant:atlas-ml).
Zoe (sre): saw that too. p95 gen latency increased ~180ms and some slab evictions. Any idea if this is noisy neighbor or a misconfigured job?
Ravi (infra): preliminary: job is using 8 GPUs per job with aggressive prefetch and forcing PCIe NVMe streaming. It's hitting host egress and host-nic queue, causing cross-tenant packet drops.
Luis (platform): can we throttle at repo-level? We have metered egress per-tenant but not per-job. We could apply a temporary soft egress cap to atlas-ml slice or nudge routing to a quieter rack.
Priya (sales-eng): atlas-ml is on a dedicated contract; they'd be upset if we throttle. Can we shift their non-SLA background jobs to preemptible without touching their prod slices?
infra-oncall: current dedicated headroom in eu-west1 is only ~10% on that pool. Preemptible warm headroom is ~25% but embedding jobs will thrash kvcache if moved.
alloc-bot: [alloc] Detected cross-tenant egress tail causing 12% packet loss on rack-42 between 09:12-09:22. (link: https://telemetry.redwood/egress/2076549999).
Zoe (sre): actionable plan: 1) isolate atlas-ml job group with QoS tag `egress-softcap=atlas-burst` and limit max-egress=150mbps, 2) route background batch jobs to `preemptible-cpu` (not warm-gpu) where possible, 3) run a canary shift for 10m.
Ravi (infra): +1 but step 2 depends on atlas engineers changing job config. we may need a forced routing rule for job-key prefixes matching `batch/emb-*`.
Luis (platform): we can implement a routing rule: `routerctl prefix add --tenant=atlas-ml --prefix=batch/emb --target=preemptible-cold --force=true --note="egress-containment-2076549999"`
Priya (sales-eng): I'll ping their TAM and suggest they mark non-urgent batch jobs with `queue:background` tag. Try gentle nudge first before force.
infra-oncall: I can apply short-lived QoS caps now in parallel: `qosctl set --tenant=atlas-ml --tag=egress-softcap --max-egress=150mbps --ttl=15m`
Zoe (sre): add `noisy-neighbor-await` annotation in the router so we don't auto-evict their dedicated slices. We prefer traffic shaping over eviction for paying tenants.
Ravi (infra): note: if packet loss persists we may still see slab churn and KV miss storm. Watch KV-eviction-rate and per-tenant retransmits.
alloc-bot: [telemetry] KV miss rate for atlas-ml increased x3 at 09:18, overall packet retransmits +27% (dash: https://telemetry.redwood/kvcache/atlas-ml).
Luis (platform): I'm concerned about embeddings thrashing cache if we move to preemptible warm. `preemptible-cold` will kill latency but preserve cache for prod. Good call.
Priya (sales-eng): customer reply: "we're running a quarterly embedding sweep, should finish in ~3h. we'll try to lower parallelism."
Zoe (sre): given that, do minimal interference: apply qos cap (infra-oncall), add routing prefix for batch to preemptible-cold (Luis), and set alert thresholds: p99 gen latency >200ms OR packet loss >5% triggers rollback to manual operator.
Ravi (infra): command I'm about to run (dry-run first):
```
qosctl set --tenant=atlas-ml --max-egress=150mbps --tag=egress-softcap --dry-run
routerctl prefix add --tenant=atlas-ml --prefix=batch/emb --target=preemptible-cold --force --dry-run
```
Zoe (sre): add annotation `notify:sales-eng@redwood` to both changes so Priya can track.
infra-oncall: dry-run CLI outputs look good. applying QoS now; will watch 5min windows.
alloc-bot: [action] QoS applied at 2026-03-23T09:30:12Z by infra-oncall (id: q-2076549999).
Ravi (infra): monitoring: p95 down to +40ms above baseline, p99 still elevated but trending down. KV miss-rate decreasing.
Zoe (sre): any sign of spillover to adjacent racks? check nvlink errors and NIC drops.
alloc-bot: [telemetry] rack-41 packet drops spiked earlier but back to baseline after QoS. nvlink errors none.
Priya (sales-eng): atlas-ml replied: "thanks, we've reduced parallelism by 40% and canceled a portion of sweep." Happy for temporary measures.
Luis (platform): I'll create a follow-up to add per-job egress metering so we can act earlier next time (ticket: PLAT-8721).
Ravi (infra): retrospective items: per-job egress limits, per-slice background routing, and better console visibility for egress headroom per-pool.
Zoe (sre): :thumbsup: write a short post-incident note with timeline and mitigations. I'll help with metrics export.
infra-oncall: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see repeat surge.
